Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

March noun

also in March

classical

Sen. Ep. 86.20: Mārtiō exāctō
Traupman 77

1Mārtius: long a (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 366, s.v. Mārs, marks Mārs and Mārtius and derives the vowel from *māwarts, with loss of w between like vowels. Traupman 77 marks it too. Ruling: Which authority settles a vowel.

Mārtius1, Mārtia, Mārtium

adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis), declension

of March; March

Mars’s month, the first of the old Roman year, which is why September to December are named seventh to tenth. Kalendae, Nōnae, Īdūs Mārtiae: the 1st, 7th and 15th.

Examples

  • Mārtis erat prīmus mēnsis, Venerisque secundus

    the first month was Mars’s, the second Venus’s (in the old Roman year)Ov. F. 1.39

  • mēnse Mārtiō

    in MarchTraupman 343

See also month, February, April, the Ides, spring.
